method: Each path frame was read on the source video (sequential decode, seek-checked: offset 0 MAD 0.0, +-1 MAD 9-16): ball (x,y,r) eye-read on a gridded crop (purple blob only on 243-277 where its circle was checked on the lane crop; the blob fails from 289 on the purple pin-deck backdrop), and in the SAME frame at the ball centre row the left/right lane edges at the wood/gutter boundary (Sobel or grey-profile step, every marker inspected on a gridded crop; from 293 on the ball row overlaps the rack, so edges are straight-line fits of the gutter lips over the 25 rows in front of the pin deck, extrapolated to the ball row); board = 1 + 38*(x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x), no quad carry-over. Entry = median of 6 named reads: edge profile at pin_hit-1/0/+1, pin ruler at f296/f297 with PHYSICAL pin geometry (7 columns at 6 in, 7-to-10 = 32.97 units of 41.5/38 in, headpin = board 20; the task text's 7->33/10->7 mapping is self-contradictory and was not used), ball-diameter ruler at f298 (2r = 7.78 units, distance from the right edge); extra keys contact_y/left_x_contact/right_x_contact/board_contact re-read the edges at the contact row y+r (board stays the row-y read).
limits: Handheld camera with 45-59 px/frame jumps around 290-300: far-end ball r 6.5-8 is read on a dark ring with a highlight, centres +-1.5 px (= +-0.7 board), r +-1 px. Far-end edges +-1.5 px from the line fits; the left gutter has a capping stripe 16-27 px outside the lip that a wide window picks up (295-299). Near-end edges on 243/260/277 were missed by the Sobel window and come from grey profiles (+-3 px). Scale disagreement at f297: lane edges 83.6 px / 38 = 2.20 px/unit, pin columns 62 px / 32.97 = 1.88 px/unit, ball 14 px / 7.78 = 1.80 px/unit; pin span / lane width 0.74 vs physical 0.87; the headpin column sits on the edge midpoint (331 vs 330.9). Ball ruler at r 7-8 is +-13 % per px of radius, the weakest read. With the task text's mapping (26 units for the 7 columns) the pin ruler would read 9.5 (f296) and 9.1 (f297). pin_hit 299 (loop 1, +-2) is NOT confirmed by pin motion: no pin moves through f305 (contact_296_305.jpg); the ball overlaps the rack in projection from ~291 because the camera is low, so the 'centre reaches the pin-base row' frame (291) is 8 frames before pin_hit.

loop1_compare: Loop-1 truth board 5.5 +-2.0 (edge reads 8.2/7.2/7.4/6.0 at f280-296, pin ruler 4.2 at f296). This path reads 7.4-8.7 over 285-300; the far-end edge reads agree with loop-1's f285-290 reads, and loop-1's lower number comes from its f296 edge read (6.0) and pin ruler (4.2). Here the pin ruler reads 6.2-6.7 with the physical span.

pin_row.note: Re-derived. Head top 475-478 raw on 10 frames, 476-477.7 camera-compensated, and read by eye at ~475 on f299 (zoom_293_304_338_472.jpg; stripes at 484-486, so it is the head top); the 434 detections on f302-307 are the masking-unit edge and were ignored. Ball bottom reaches the base at f304 (f303 +1.4), centre at f302. contact_frame - k = 310, 6 frames later. Pin ruler: f301 columns (headpin 349, 10.0 px per 6 in) moved by camera dx +5.6 to f304.
pin_row.note_prev: NOT re-derived; kept 291 from the existing truth, flagged as early. On zoom_299_314_365_508.jpg the ball is in front of the standing rack at f299-302, first overlapped by front pins at f303, and the first pin moves at f312, 21 frames after 291. As on 191913/191253 the base row 527 is most likely the bottom of the deck reflection; the contact point probably reaches the head row around f302-303 (first occlusion), not measured; WITHDRAWN: a ball cannot sit behind front pins without touching one, so that "occlusion" is 2D overlap; use est_60ft_frame_from_contact instead. The existing path has no point at f291 in the last frames read, so no board is recorded.
pin_row.method: pin-height base: headpin-column pin top (head top, not the neck stripe) + 15 in x lane px/in at the base row + 3.5 px (topmost white is the 5-pin, 20.8 in behind), per frame where detected within 6 px of the camera-compensated top, else compensated top + measured camera dy; ball centre from the path or a tracked purple component, r = geometric radius scaled by lane width; frame_contact_row = first frame with (y + r) - base <= +1 px.
pin_row.est_60ft_note: contact_frame - k, k=2 = rack row of the first pin within 6.1 units of the ball's board (about 1 frame per row); first visible pin motion lags the touch, so this is an upper bound

contact_note: Ball behind the front pins f303-311 with pins upright; pins beside the ball lean and blur at f312, falling f313 (zoom_299_314_365_508.jpg). Aligned change 10.9 (f311) -> 17.0 (f312). +-1. This is 13 frames after the cut pin_hit 299.

exit.deflection: entered well right of the pocket (board ~7.5), missed the headpin, and was lost at the head row; the path through the deck was not seen
exit.note: ball lost at the head row: frame and board are the last-visible position at deck entry (exit is contact_frame + 0/1, too soon to cross 2.85 ft of deck); the true exit was not seen

exit_method: Ball read by eye on 5x camera-followed gridded crops (zoom_299_314_365_508.jpg) and matched to the moving purple component; lane edges are the wood-to-gutter Sobel step on rows 513-554 in front of the deck in the exit frame itself (rms 0.29-0.43 px), evaluated at the ball row. Pin ruler: 7 columns 325..384 at f305 (9.83 px per 6 in, headpin 356) moved to f313 by the measured camera dx.
exit_limits: Edge lines are extrapolated 50-90 px to the ball row. From f313 the ball component widens (28-42 px) as it merges with the dark pit exposed behind the falling pins, and the 31-36 px component on f315-318 is static in camera-compensated coordinates, so it was not counted; exit is +-1. The f312 -> f313 edge reads differ by 1.9 boards for a ball that barely moved, which is the edge-read noise at this row.
